transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Well, I've been having trouble going to the toilet. I'm opening my bowels much less often than usual, and when I do, I have to strain quite a bit.
When did you first notice that going to the toilet became harder?
It started about three weeks ago. Before that I was going every day or every other day, but now it's more like every four or five days.
Have you ever had an allergy or a bad reaction to any medicine?
No, I've never had any allergies to medicines as far as I know.
How much is this trouble with going to the toilet affecting your daily life?
The straining is uncomfortable, I'd say about a 4 out of 10, and my lower tummy feels bloated. It's worrying me, and I'd really like something to get things moving.
Have you started any new medicines or changed any of your usual ones recently?
Yes, I started a new painkiller about a month ago called co-codamol 30/500 — two tablets four times a day — for my back pain. My other medicines I've been on for a while and haven't changed.
Have you noticed anything that seems to make it easier or harder to go to the toilet?
I have been drinking less than I used to — only about three cups of tea a day — because I don't want to keep getting up in the night. That may have made things harder.

Other than your back pain, is there anything else about your past health, like other health problems that have lasted a while, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays, that you think I should know?
Yes, I have osteoarthritis in my spine and my knees. I also have an irregular heartbeat — atrial fibrillation.
Is there anything else you've noticed along with this that we haven't talked about yet?
No, I haven't seen any blood in my stools, nothing black, and I haven't been vomiting. Just the bloating and the straining.
Is there anything else about your past health that you think I should know?
I think that's the main things — the arthritis and the irregular heartbeat. For my medicines, besides the co-codamol, I take apixaban, bisoprolol, and a calcium and vitamin D tablet.
Are there any other medicines you take, even ones you buy yourself or only use now and then, that we haven't talked about yet?
No, I don't take anything else — no medicines I buy myself or use now and then.
Have you noticed any changes in your daily activities since you started having trouble going to the toilet?
No, I can't say I've noticed any change in what I do day to day. It's mainly the discomfort and the worry about it.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
